description: Ask the user for a secret (a password, an API key, a token) and have Wisp type it straight into a running process. A box opens where the user types or pastes it; you never see it and it never enters this conversation or the session log, so use this instead of asking in the chat. Give the number of the process that will read it. For a program that asks at a prompt (sudo, ssh, a login), run it with bash and tty, and call this once it waits at its prompt with echo off: the secret is typed and Enter pressed. For a command that reads the secret from standard input, such as wisp account add NAME --key-stdin or a password manager's command line, start it with bash and run_in_background, without tty, then call this with end_input true. For a command that wants the secret in an environment variable or inside other text, start a short script the same way that reads one line and passes it on (IFS= read -r S; TOKEN="$S" exec the-command), and call this without end_input, since the script reads a whole line; never use one that puts the secret on a command line or prints it. If the result says the terminal would show what is typed, start the command again without tty so that it reads standard input; don't ask the user to take the terminal over for a secret. Make this the last call of your reply: calls after it in the same reply are not run. The result says only whether the secret was typed, never what it was.

end_input.description: Close the process's input after the secret, with no line break, for a command that reads standard input to its end. Defaults to false: the secret is followed by Enter.

name.description: What you are asking for, in a few words, shown as the box's title, such as "sudo password" or "OpenAI API key". At most 40 characters.

process.description: The number of the running process that reads the secret.

reason.description: One sentence shown to the user: why it is needed and what will be done with it. At most 200 characters.

show_end.description: How many characters at the end of a pasted secret the box shows. Defaults to 0.

show_start.description: How many characters at the start of a pasted secret the box shows, so the user can check it is the right one. Leave this and show_end out for a password or passphrase: the box then shows only stars. For a key or token with a public prefix, give the prefix's length here (8 for sk-proj-) and 4 in show_end. For one with no public prefix, give 0 here and 4 in show_end. Wisp shows less when the secret is short, and only stars for one typed by hand. Defaults to 0.

name: ask_secret
